study.title: Luke 22 The Passover, the institution of supper and the imminent passion of Jesus
study.overview: Luke 22 presents the approach of Christ's passion in four main movements: the conspiracy of the authorities and the betrayal of Judas; the preparation and celebration of the Passover, in which Jesus institutes supper as a memorial of his death; the instructions to the disciples on service, perseverance and spiritual danger; and, finally, the anguish in Gethsemane, the prison, the denial of Peter and the religious judgment that leads to the formal accusation against Jesus. The chapter shows that the death of Jesus is not an accident, but it happens within the purpose of God, while at the same time revealing the real human guilt of Judas, the leaders and weakness of the disciples.

outline.title: Conspiracy and betrayal
outline.explanation: Religious leaders seek to kill Jesus with political prudence, fearing the people. Judas is influenced by Satan, negotiates with the chief priests and seeks a discreet occasion to deliver Jesus.

outline.title: Easter prepared and supper instituted
outline.explanation: Jesus guides the preparation of the Passover, eats with the twelve and announces the character of his near death. In the bread and cup, he establishes a memorial of his surrender, shedding his blood as a new covenant for them.

outline.title: Present traitor, inverted greatness and warning to Peter
outline.explanation: Jesus reveals that the traitor is at table and states that his death fulfills the plan determined by God. Then correct the dispute for superiority among the disciples, promises kingdom and future responsibility, and warns Peter of the sieve of Satan and the denial that will come.

outline.title: Gethsemane, Prisoner, Denial and Religious Condemnity
outline.explanation: On the Mount of Olives, Jesus speaks submissively to the Father, is strengthened and goes to meet the prison. Judas identifies him with a kiss, Jesus heals the wounded, denounces the hour of darkness, and the disciples abandon him, while Peter denies him. The chapter ends with the insults, the gathering of the council and the confession of Jesus as the Son of man at the right hand of God's power, leading the leaders to consider sufficient testimony against him.

study.context: The chapter places the events in the feast of unleavened bread, also called Easter, linked to the paschal sacrifice. Notes indicate that this period included the pascal meal and then the days of the party. The text uses this frame to show that God's deliverance in behalf of Israel finds its fulfillment in Jesus, which is delivered just at that time and interprets his death as a saving act.
study.theology: Luke 22 teaches that the cross of Christ is both human injustice and fulfillment of God's sovereign purpose. Judas acts for real betrayal, the leaders act for fear and calculus, and Peter fails for weakness; yet, Jesus states that this was determined and must be fulfilled. The supper connects Jesus" death to the new covenant: his body is given and his blood is shed in favor of the disciples, for the continual memory of the church. The chapter also redefines greatness as a service, showing Jesus as the true model of humble authority. Moreover, prayer in suffering reveals filial obedience: Jesus desires that the will of the Father will prevail, without denying the intensity of his anguish. Finally, judgment before the council exposes the spiritual blindness of the leaders, which transform the true confession of Jesus into a charge of guilt.

scholarViews.insight: The expression "redetermined" indicates that although ungodly men betrayed and killed Jesus, this was included in God's sovereign plan to accomplish salvation.
The preparation of the Passover shows Christ entering the moment marked by God, and not by chance; his surrender occurs at the very time when redemption is finished.
The testimony heard by the counsel is understood as a confirmation of Jesus' claim to be the Son of God, and therefore they treat him as blasphemy and continue to condemn him.

questions: What does Luke 22 teach me about the relationship between God's sovereignty and human responsibility for sin?
In which areas have I sought greatness, instead of serving as Jesus taught the disciples?
How does Jesus" prayer in Gethsemane correct my tendency to avoid suffering at any cost?
study.practice: This week, read Luke 22 in prayer and observe three practical answers: confess any sin of betrayal, pride or denial; participate in the Lord's supper with reverence, remembering that Christ gave himself up for you; and choose a concrete gesture of humble service, especially in a relationship or task in which you would normally seek recognition. Also, take a time of prayer with sincerity, asking for strength to submit your will to God's will.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided do not detail all possible historical and theological aspects, so the study avoids affirming data not explicitly supported. There are also differences of emphasis between commentators, especially on the scene of supper, the presence of Judas and the meaning of Jesus" agony; these readings were treated as interpretations, not as absolute conclusions.
